rust.name: crates/sqlite/src/schema.rs:210:5: replace give_back with ()
rust.why: Writes can return correct results while leaving freed pages in the file, so a test must observe page reclamation to catch this.

rust.name: crates/sqlite/src/schema.rs:193:5: replace make_incremental -> rusqlite::Result<()> with Ok(())
rust.why: A legacy database can migrate and serve reads and writes while still retaining its original auto_vacuum mode.

rust.name: crates/sqlite/src/schema.rs:177:14: replace > with >= in migrate
rust.why: This rejects an already current database, which fresh opens and upgrades from older versions do not exercise.

rust.name: crates/sqlite/src/schema.rs:193:74: replace != with == in make_incremental
rust.why: This runs a full VACUUM on already incremental files, which can leave all query results and the final auto_vacuum mode unchanged.
